name: DNS Resolution Failure
symptoms: cannot open websites by domain name
can ping IP address but not website name
server IP address could not be found
likely_causes: Configured DNS server is unreachable or offline
Incorrect DNS IP address configured on client or router
Local DNS cache is corrupted
diagnostic_steps: Run nslookup google.com to see if your DNS server responds.
Ping 8.8.8.8 to verify if raw IP connectivity works.
Check your network adapter settings to see what DNS addresses are assigned.
fix_steps: Set your primary DNS server to 1.1.1.1 and secondary to 8.8.8.8.
Flush your local DNS cache by running ipconfig /flushdns in the terminal.
Restart your router if it acts as the local DNS relay.

name: Incorrect Default Gateway
symptoms: can reach local devices but no internet
local network works but external sites fail
likely_causes: Manual static IP setup with a typo in the gateway IP
DHCP server provided wrong gateway option 3
Subnet mismatch between client IP and gateway IP
diagnostic_steps: Run ipconfig or ip route show to find your active default gateway.
Ping the default gateway IP address directly.
Check if your IP address and gateway IP share the same network prefix.
fix_steps: Switch your network adapter to obtain IP settings automatically via DHCP.
If using static IP, update your default gateway to match your router's actual LAN IP.
Verify that your subnet mask matches your local router network.

name: Ethernet Duplex Mismatch
symptoms: link speed drops to 10 or 100 megabits half duplex
high collision count on switch port
likely_causes: One side of the link is forced to full duplex while the other is set to auto-negotiate
Faulty network driver reverting to half-duplex fallback
Old unmanaged switch incapable of auto-negotiation
diagnostic_steps: Check Ethernet link status and duplex mode in device adapter properties.
Inspect switch port error counters for late collisions and CRC errors.
Test transfer speeds between two wired hosts on the same switch.
fix_steps: Set both the client adapter and switch port to Auto-Negotiation.
If auto-negotiation fails, hardcode both ends to 1000 Mbps Full Duplex.
Update your network interface card driver.

name: VLAN Tagging Misconfiguration
symptoms: wired port gets no DHCP lease
cannot see office servers from port
likely_causes: Access port assigned to the wrong VLAN ID
Trunk port between switches not allowing the required VLAN
PVID or native VLAN mismatch causing frames to drop
diagnostic_steps: Verify the switch port VLAN assignment for the connected wall jack.
Confirm if trunk links allow tagged traffic for this VLAN ID.
Check if DHCP relay or helper address is enabled on the VLAN interface.
fix_steps: Reassign the access port to the correct VLAN ID on the switch.
Ensure trunk links allow the specific VLAN tag.
Renew your client IP address after correcting the port VLAN.

name: DHCP Scope Pool Exhaustion
symptoms: new devices cannot get IP address
guest wifi not giving ip addresses
likely_causes: All available IP addresses in the DHCP pool are leased out
DHCP lease time is set too long for high-turnover guest networks
IP lease leakage caused by abandoned virtual machines or guest devices
diagnostic_steps: Look at client IP to see if it starts with 169.254.
Log in to router or DHCP server and inspect active lease count.
Check DHCP scope range and subnet mask capacity.
fix_steps: Expand the DHCP scope range or enlarge the subnet mask.
Reduce DHCP lease time to 2 or 4 hours for transient devices.
Clear stale DHCP leases on the router or DHCP server.

name: Excessive Network Latency
likely_causes: Local link congestion from background downloads or cloud backups
Suboptimal routing hop or peering bottleneck along ISP route
Wireless interference or excessive distance from access point
diagnostic_steps: Run traceroute or tracert to identify which hop introduces latency.
Ping your local router IP to check if the lag is inside your LAN.
Monitor bandwidth usage on local devices to see who is saturating the link.
fix_steps: Enable Quality of Service QoS on your router to prioritize interactive traffic.
Pause large background downloads, torrents, or cloud synchronization.
Connect via an Ethernet cable instead of Wi-Fi for testing.

name: Network Packet Loss
likely_causes: Overloaded router CPU or buffer overflow
Damaged network cable or loose RJ45 connector
RF interference or weak Wi-Fi signal
diagnostic_steps: Run ping 8.8.8.8 -n 50 to measure the exact packet loss percentage.
Ping your local router simultaneously to isolate LAN vs WAN loss.
Check router CPU and memory utilization in the management portal.
fix_steps: Replace the Ethernet cable connecting the computer or modem.
Move closer to your Wi-Fi router or switch to the 5 GHz band.
Reboot your router and modem to clear buffer congestion.

name: Duplicate IP Address Conflict
symptoms: intermittent network disconnects every few seconds
windows warning another device using your ip address
likely_causes: Static IP configured inside the active DHCP dynamic lease pool
Two devices manually assigned the exact same IP address
Rogue or secondary router offering overlapping IP leases
diagnostic_steps: Check event viewer or system logs for IP conflict notifications.
Disconnect your device and ping your IP from another machine to see if it replies.
Check the ARP table using arp -a to see if the MAC address alternates.
fix_steps: Switch the conflicting device to receive an IP via DHCP.
Change static IP to an address outside the active DHCP distribution pool.
Reserve static IP bindings via DHCP reservations on the router.

name: Incorrect Subnet Mask
symptoms: can communicate with some local PCs but not others
cannot see network printer on same subnet
one way traffic on local lan
likely_causes: Typo in manual subnet mask like 255.255.0.0 instead of 255.255.255.0
Mismatched CIDR prefix on static IP configurations
Inconsistent subnet configuration between router interface and hosts
diagnostic_steps: Compare subnet masks on two machines on the same local network.
Calculate the valid host range for your IP and subnet mask.
Attempt to ping an adjacent host that shares the intended subnet.
fix_steps: Correct the subnet mask in adapter settings to match your router network.
Switch to DHCP to pull the verified subnet configuration automatically.
Verify subnet settings across all static devices on the LAN.

name: Wi-Fi Radio Frequency Interference
symptoms: wifi speeds drop near kitchen or appliances
high packet drop on wireless but wired is fine
likely_causes: Neighboring access points broadcasting on the same 2.4 GHz channel
Physical interference from microwaves, Bluetooth, or thick concrete walls
Too many devices competing for airtime on an old 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 4 band
diagnostic_steps: Run a Wi-Fi analyzer app to inspect channel congestion around you.
Test network throughput over a wired Ethernet cable to verify the baseline.
Check if issues disappear when standing 5 feet from the router.
fix_steps: Switch your devices to the 5 GHz or 6 GHz Wi-Fi frequency band.
Change 2.4 GHz router channel manually to 1, 6, or 11.
Relocate the wireless access point away from metal objects and appliances.

name: Maximum Transmission Unit MTU Mismatch
symptoms: can ping hosts and open small web pages but large sites hang
vpn disconnects on large file transfers
packet needs to be fragmented but DF set
likely_causes: Client MTU exceeds VPN or PPPoE tunnel capacity
Path MTU discovery failing due to ICMP Type 3 Code 4 blocked by firewall
Jumbo frames configured on one switch port but not end-to-end
diagnostic_steps: Run ping google.com -f -l 1472 to test maximum unfragmented packet size.
Reduce packet size incrementally until ping replies without fragmentation error.
Inspect MTU setting on client network interface and VPN adapter.
fix_steps: Lower client or router MTU to 1420 for VPN connections or 1492 for PPPoE.
Enable MSS clamping on the border router or firewall.
Ensure ICMP fragmentation needed messages are not blocked.

name: ARP Cache Poisoning or Stale Entry
symptoms: stale mac address in arp table
cannot communicate with gateway after hardware change
likely_causes: Router or server replaced but client cached the old MAC address
Rogue host running ARP spoofing or gratuitous ARP attacks
IP migration between virtual machine hosts without gratuitous ARP
diagnostic_steps: Run arp -a to inspect the local ARP cache table.
Check if the gateway IP is mapped to an unfamiliar MAC address.
Verify if duplicate MAC addresses exist for different IP entries.
fix_steps: Flush the ARP cache by running netsh interface ip delete arpcache or arp -d *.
Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection DAI on managed switches.
Restart the network adapter to refresh local address tables.

name: Firewall Blocking Application Port
symptoms: web browsing works but specific application cannot connect
port connection refused or timed out
email client cannot send or receive
game cannot connect to multiplayer server
likely_causes: Host operating system firewall blocking incoming or outgoing port
Corporate or ISP perimeter firewall dropping traffic on non-standard ports
Antivirus software inspecting and dropping application socket
diagnostic_steps: Run Test-NetConnection -ComputerName target.com -Port 443 in PowerShell.
Temporarily check firewall logs for dropped outbound packets.
Test if the same application connects when using an alternate network.
fix_steps: Create an outbound firewall rule permitting the required port.
Ensure your router port forwarding is configured if hosting a service.
Check that your antivirus network shield has not quarantined the app.

name: Damaged or Loose Ethernet Cable
symptoms: link light flashing intermittently or dark
speed drops from 1 Gbps to 100 Mbps
likely_causes: Broken retaining clip on RJ45 connector causing loose contact
Pin wire fracture inside twisted pair cable due to bending or crushing
Poorly crimped patch cable with loose pair termination
diagnostic_steps: Inspect the physical RJ45 plastic clip on both ends of the cable.
Look at the link indicator LED on both the computer and switch port.
Test with a hardware cable tester or swap in a known good cable.
fix_steps: Unplug and firmly reseat the Ethernet connector until it clicks.
Replace the Ethernet cable with a verified Category 6 patch cord.
Try plugging into a different switch port on the router.

name: Spanning Tree Protocol STP Loop
symptoms: switch activity lights flashing furiously in unison
instant freeze when plugging patch cable
likely_causes: Two switch ports accidentally cross-connected creating a loop
Spanning Tree Protocol disabled on one or more managed switches
Bridge Protocol Data Unit BPDU filter misconfigured on access ports
diagnostic_steps: Look for high frequency flashing on all switch port LEDs simultaneously.
Disconnect newly connected cables one by one to see if network restores.
Review switch console for Spanning Tree topology change notifications.
fix_steps: Immediately disconnect the redundant loop cable between switch ports.
Enable Spanning Tree Protocol RSTP or MSTP on all active switches.
Enable BPDU Guard and Loop Guard on all user facing access ports.

name: Rogue DHCP Server on LAN
symptoms: computers getting weird IP addresses like 192.168.0.x instead of 10.0.x.x
sudden internet loss across several office computers
default gateway pointing to a personal router or printer
likely_causes: Someone plugged a home Wi-Fi router into an office wall jack using the LAN port
Virtual machine hypervisor running default NAT DHCP service on bridged network
Misconfigured secondary test server handing out leases
diagnostic_steps: Run ipconfig /all to inspect which DHCP Server IP provided the lease.
Trace the MAC address of the rogue DHCP IP using the switch MAC address table.
Check which switch port learned the offending MAC address.
fix_steps: Locate and unplug the unauthorized router or service from the network.
Enable DHCP Snooping on all managed switches to block rogue offers.
Renew client IP configurations with ipconfig /renew.

name: Captive Portal Redirection Failure
symptoms: connected to hotel or airport wifi but no internet
browser displays certificate security warning instead of login page
captive portal login page does not load
likely_causes: Browser attempting HTTPS connection before portal authentication
Custom DNS server like 1.1.1.1 configured preventing portal DNS hijacking
Strict DNS over HTTPS DoH enabled in browser bypassing captive portal
diagnostic_steps: Attempt navigating to an unencrypted HTTP website like http://neverssl.com.
Check if your DNS is set to automatic DHCP instead of a manual IP.
Disable third party VPN applications during the login handshake.
fix_steps: Open your browser and navigate to http://neverssl.com or http://1.1.1.1.
Temporarily turn off VPN and private DNS settings until signed in.
Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network to trigger the login popup.

name: Stale or Poisoned Local DNS Cache
symptoms: website loads old IP address after migration
browser shows outdated version of site while phone loads new site
site migrated but still pointing to old server
likely_causes: Operating system cached old DNS record before TTL expired
Browser internal DNS cache retaining stale IP mapping
Local hosts file contains outdated manual IP overrides
diagnostic_steps: Run ipconfig /displaydns to search for the specific domain name.
Check your operating system hosts file for hardcoded entries.
Test domain resolution using nslookup with an external server like 8.8.8.8.
fix_steps: Run ipconfig /flushdns in the command prompt to clear system cache.
Clear host cache in Chrome at chrome://net-internals/#dns.
Remove any manual entries in the hosts file and restart your browser.

name: Bufferbloat Queue Latency Spike
symptoms: ping spikes to 500ms whenever someone downloads a game or uploads a video
rubberbanding during online gaming while stream is uploading
likely_causes: Router buffers oversized queues during heavy upload or download saturation
Lack of modern queue management like CAKE or FQ-CoDel on home router
Asymmetric broadband connection maxing out upload bandwidth
diagnostic_steps: Run a bufferbloat test at waveform.com while monitoring ping latency.
Run a continuous ping while starting a full-speed upload test.
Check router QoS settings to see if active queue management is enabled.
fix_steps: Enable Smart Queue Management SQM like CAKE or FQ-CoDel on your router.
Cap upload bandwidth in router QoS to 90 percent of your ISP maximum speed.
Limit concurrent upload streams on file sharing or cloud backup applications.

name: ISP Upstream Gateway Outage
symptoms: router shows wan disconnected or optical los light red
can ping local router but no internet IP can be reached
likely_causes: Physical fiber or coaxial line cut upstream in neighborhood
ISP local distribution node maintenance or power failure
Modem lost synchronization with ISP headend equipment
diagnostic_steps: Look at the WAN or Internet status LED on your modem and router.
Log into router admin page to verify if WAN IP address is 0.0.0.0.
Check your mobile phone carrier data to see if ISP reports a regional outage.
fix_steps: Power cycle your modem and router by unplugging power for 30 seconds.
Inspect the coaxial or fiber cable entering the modem for physical bends.
Call your Internet Service Provider to check for regional service interruptions.
